business_summary: Trimble Inc. is a US, NASDAQ-listed (TRMB) positioning and field-technology company whose Unity Remote Monitoring and Raven-Eye radar flowmeter products measure water flow and level in real time. That product line is the mapped exposure to the tibet-mega-dam chain's riparian-risk-monitoring link, sold as flood- and overflow-monitoring infrastructure rather than as a project-specific supplier to the dam itself.

exposure_summary.narrative: Trimble sits on riparian-risk-monitoring, scored QUIET. The company's own 2020 product release documents real-time water-flow and level monitoring aimed at reducing flooding and sewer overflows, matching the link's own note that demand is real (India built new monitoring posts post-announcement) but revenue concentration per listed name is unproven; no Tibet-basin-specific or dam-specific revenue is disclosed or sourced, and this is one product line inside a much larger positioning and field-technology business.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: no revenue percentage tied to the tibet-mega-dam exposure is sourced for Trimble this run; the flow-monitoring product line is not broken out in companyfacts segment data. See data_gaps.

crowdedness_caveats: Trimble sits on a link scored QUIET (see placements above); the link's own note flags unproven per-name revenue concentration across the whole link.

data/market/TRMB.json carries no pcs (positioning/crowdedness-signal) block, so this profile cannot independently corroborate the link-level crowdedness score with issuer-level analyst-coverage or institutional-ownership figures.
Water-flow monitoring is a small, undisclosed slice of Trimble's much larger positioning, agriculture, and construction-technology business; the metrics below are company-wide, not segment-specific.

risks.claim: Piotroski F-score 4 (state MIDDLING): the model fails five of nine criteria (year-over-year ROA change, accruals quality, leverage change, current-ratio change, asset turnover), a mixed quality read rather than a strong one.

The large FY2025-to-FY2026 net-income swing (1,504,400,000 to 424,000,000) is not explained by any line item in the local store; a filing read would be needed to attribute it.

latest_fy.source_name: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts, read from data/market/TRMB.json fundamentals (source sec-companyfacts)

revenue_cagr_3y.source_name: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts, read from data/market/TRMB.json fundamentals (source sec-companyfacts)
revenue_cagr_3y.basis: Three-year compound annual revenue growth computed as (3587300000 / 3676300000) ** (1/3) - 1 from the companyfacts Revenues series, fiscal year ended 2022-12-30 to fiscal year ended 2026-01-02. Revenue is essentially flat to slightly down over the window (peaked at 3798700000 in fiscal 2023).

operating_margin.source_name: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts, read from data/market/TRMB.json fundamentals (source sec-companyfacts)
operating_margin.basis: Operating income 592000000 divided by revenue 3587300000 for the fiscal year ended 2026-01-02, both from companyfacts.

fcf_margin.source_name: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts, read from data/market/TRMB.json fundamentals (source sec-companyfacts)
fcf_margin.basis: Operating cash flow 386200000 minus capital expenditure 25300000, divided by revenue 3587300000, for the fiscal year ended 2026-01-02, all from companyfacts. operating_cash_flow_to_net_income (0.911) is omitted as redundant given the schema requires only one of the two fields; fcf_margin is the more standard cross-issuer comparison.

net_debt_to_ebitda.source_name: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts, read from data/market/TRMB.json fundamentals (source sec-companyfacts)
net_debt_to_ebitda.basis: Net debt 1228500000 (total debt 1442900000 as of 2026-07-03 less cash 214400000 as of 2026-07-03) divided by an EBITDA proxy 791900000 (operating income 592000000 plus depreciation 199900000 for the fiscal year ended 2026-01-02). The debt/cash reading is a later quarterly point than the FY-end EBITDA inputs it is netted against.

piotroski.source_name: Upstream market store data/market/TRMB.json quality, computed over SEC EDGAR companyfacts with financetoolkit.models
piotroski.basis: Piotroski F-score 4 (state MIDDLING, 9 of 9 inputs found), computed over SEC companyfacts statements in data/market/TRMB.json quality.piotroski.

beneish_state.source_name: Upstream market store data/market/TRMB.json quality, computed over SEC EDGAR companyfacts with financetoolkit.models
beneish_state.basis: Beneish M-score -2.24 against the -1.78 threshold, earnings-manipulation state CLEAN (12 of 12 inputs found), computed over SEC companyfacts statements in data/market/TRMB.json quality.beneish. A more negative M-score is the non-manipulator reading.

market_cap.basis: Market capitalization 14145840000.0 = SEC companyfacts share count 236000000 (fiscal year ended 2026-01-02) multiplied by the close 59.94 of 2026-08-31; the close is the repo's own dual-source market plane (data/market/TRMB.json, price_status AGREED), not an issuer document.

price_to_sales.source_name: Upstream market store data/market/TRMB.json quality.derived.market_cap over SEC companyfacts revenue
price_to_sales.basis: Market capitalization 14145840000.0 divided by fiscal year 2026-01-02 revenue 3587300000.

implied_fcf_cagr.basis: Free-cash-flow CAGR the current enterprise value 15374340000.0 implies over a 5-year explicit period on base FCF 360900000, solved by bisection at a 0.09 discount rate and 0.025 terminal growth. Assumption-dependent expectation reading, not a reported figure.

horizon_spread.basis: Spread between the implied CAGR solved over the shortest and longest explicit periods (5y: 0.2742, 7y: 0.2055, 10y: 0.1566) in quality.reverse_dcf.implied_by_horizon; inherits the same assumed discount rate and terminal growth.

confidence_audit.basis: Counts cover the canonical metric fields only (cash_conversion writes only fcf_margin, valuation writes market_cap and price_to_sales). VERIFIED is the one figure read directly off SEC companyfacts as reported (latest_fy revenue). INFERRED covers figures computed from companyfacts or the market store's quality block with the derivation named in each basis (growth, margins, cash_conversion, leverage, quality x2, valuation x2). SPECULATIVE covers the two reverse-DCF fields, which rest on an assumed discount rate and terminal growth rather than a reported figure. No canonical field is NULL.
